blocks.text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterised by insulin resistance and progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction, resulting in persistent hyperglycaemia.
Management involves individualised glycaemic control, cardiovascular and renal risk reduction, weight management, prevention of complications, and appropriate pharmacological treatment.

blocks.text: Glucose lowering alone is not sufficient to prevent all diabetes-related complications.
Additional treatment may include:
Blood pressure management: ACE inhibitors or ARBs are particularly useful in selected patients with hypertension and albuminuria.
Lipid management: Statin therapy is recommended for many adults with T2DM according to age, cardiovascular risk and established ASCVD.
Antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin is indicated for appropriate secondary prevention, but not routinely for every patient with diabetes.
Kidney protection: Consider SGLT2 inhibitors, appropriate renin–angiotensin system blockade and, in selected patients with persistent albuminuria, finerenone.
Finerenone requires potassium and renal function monitoring and should not be prescribed indiscriminately.
